title: 1.011 - Define Python and Rust solver parity
author: gardusi-gustavo-bot

legacy.original_title: 1.0 - Define Python and Rust solver parity
legacy.body:
## Summary

Define how the Python solver and the Rust engine stay equivalent.

## Context

`bots/solver/solver.py` and `test_solver.py` exist, while the Rust core is a
scaffold. Two implementations will drift unless parity is defined.

## Expected outcome

- Shared fixtures: puzzles and expected results.
- The same validity and uniqueness rules on both sides.
- A parity test that runs both implementations.
- A documented source of truth for accepted solutions.
- A failure mode when the two disagree.

## Out of scope

- Choosing one language for everything.
- Performance optimization.
- Training a learned solver.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fixtures are shared by both solvers.
- [ ] Both produce the same solution for every fixture.
- [ ] Both agree on valid, invalid, and ambiguous puzzles.
- [ ] Disagreement fails CI.
- [ ] The source of truth is documented.

## Plan

- [ ] Move fixtures to a shared directory.
- [ ] Define the fixture schema.
- [ ] Add the Rust parity test.
- [ ] Run both in CI.
- [ ] Document the rules.

## Validation

- [ ] Mutating a fixture fails parity.
- [ ] Both reject a duplicate clue.
- [ ] Both accept the same valid puzzle.

## References

- Game contract: #3
- Generator: #4
- Tests: ops/templates#34
